cohort: 280 low-risk women with uncomplicated singleton pregnancies at a rural teaching hospital in Mandya, Karnataka, India
finding: Elective induction of labor at 39 weeks gestation was associated with a decrease in cesarean birth and operative delivery and improved neonatal outcomes compared to induction at 40 weeks.
mod_finding: Induction at 39 weeks was associated with a decreased likelihood of cesarean birth (17.7% versus 23.7%) and a comparable increase in rate of operative vaginal birth (9.2% vs 10.7%).
